snippets: When looking at the author lists for NeurIPS 2023 papers, one thing immediately jumps off the page: the number of authors per paper. In 2023, the average paper had 4.98 authors, as compared to 4.66 authors in 2022. Extending the analysis over the past 10 years, the trendline is clear.

It turns out that this is not the case. The NeurIPS 2023 paper with the most authors was ClimSim: A large multi-scale dataset for hybrid physics-ML climate emulation— a physics-ML crossover no less! More importantly, the entire distribution of author counts shifts right from 2022 to 2023.

Another trend which has been growing in popularity is the introduction (read creation) of acronyms in machine learning paper titles. For NeurIPS papers, the fad isn’t as omnipresent as we saw for CVPR 2023 papers. In 2023, 22% of papers introduced their own acronym, up from 18% in 2022. To see firsthand how rare this practice used to be, I encourage you to look at the titles of papers from NeurIPS 2014!
